key_insight: A matrix-free, high-order phase-field fracture solver on GPUs can efficiently capture steep crack-damage gradients while coupling visco-elastoplastic inelasticity and fracture at homogenized length scales.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable micromechanical testing simulations of damaged inelastic materials with improved performance on modern HPC systems, supporting more realistic fracture prediction in complex microstructures.
method: Implemented the Peric & Dettmer visco-elastoplastic constitutive framework in an open-source solid mechanics library.
Used matrix-free operators with high-order finite elements and p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs.
Added a rheological fracture element in series to separate inelastic and fracture effects at the homogenization scale.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical tensile and compressive simulations on synthetic particle-matrix microstructures that reproduce characteristic inelastic responses and crack propagation patterns.
watch_item: Performance and robustness may depend on high-order discretization, GPU/multigrid tuning, and careful calibration of the coupled rheological fracture model.
paper_title: Matrix-free phase-field modeling of fracture in micromechanical testing simulations of inelastic materials
